away.name: Dylan Garand
away.news: Garand had a forgettable performance last week, allowing four goals on 13 shots (.692 SV%) in a 7-1 loss to the New Jersey Devils, but has otherwise been outstanding after filling in for Igor Shesterkin, who suffered a season-ending injury. The Rangers enter Thursday's action as slight -106 road favourites against a Toronto Maple Leafs team that has outscored opponents 9-3 in their last two games (2-0-0).

home.name: Sergei Bobrovsky
home.news: The Maple Leafs are riding their first winning streak of the season and hope to extend it to three games on Thursday against the New York Rangers, with Bobrovsky between the pipes. away.name: Cooper Black

home.name: Arturs Silovs
home.news: The Penguins, losers of four straight (0-4-0), hope to rebound on Thursday, turning to Silovs in net. The Penguins enter Thursday's matchup as slight -113 home favourites against a Florida Panthers team coming off a 5-1 loss to the Ottawa Senators last night.

away.name: Darcy Kuemper
away.news: After finishing his first season with the Kings in 2024-25 as the second Vezina Trophy runner-up, Kuemper followed it with a disappointing 2025-26 season, posting a 2.78 GAA and .891 SV% in 50 games (19-14-15). Kuemper's start to the 2026-27 season hasn't been overly encouraging, but he is coming off a strong performance, saving 30 of 32 shots (.938 SV%) in a 5-2 win over the Washington Capitals. The veteran 36-year-old goalie has a 3.94 GAA and .869 SV% in five games (1-3-1). The Kings enter Thursday's game as -108 road favourites against a New York Islanders team on a two-game winning streak.

home.name: Semyon Varlamov
home.news: After being sidelined from November 2024 until the start of this season, the Islanders have used Varlamov sparingly, but he will return to the crease for his third start on Thursday. The veteran 38-year-old goalie showed some rust in his return to action, allowing three goals on 22 shots (.864 SV%) in a 5-2 loss to the New York Rangers, but had an encouraging performance in his second outing, saving 19 of 20 shots (.950 SV%) in a 2-1 shootout loss to the Ottawa Senators. The Islanders enter Thursday's action as slight -113 home favourites against a 1-4-2 Los Angeles Kings team that is coming off their first win of the season.

away.name: Adin Hill
away.news: Hill saw limited action in the latter half of last season and into the playoffs as Carter Hart became the team's go-to guy between the pipes, but Hill returns to the crease Thursday for his fifth start in 10 games. The Golden Knights enter Thursday's contest as -126 road favourites against a St. Louis Blues team that has scored just four goals in their last two games (1-1-0).

home.name: Joel Hofer
home.news: Hofer delivered a dazzling 25-save shutout in the Blues' season opener, validating Head Coach Jim Montgomery's decision to bench veteran Jordan Binnington, but Hofer has been inconsistent since. That said, the 26-year-old Hofer is coming off a tremendous performance, saving 32 of 33 shots (.919 SV%) in a 2-1 win over the Winnipeg Jets. He has a 2.19 GAA and .919 SV% in six games (3-2-1). The Blues enter Thursday's matchup as +113 home underdogs against a Vegas Golden Knights team coming off a disappointing 6-2 loss to the Tampa Bay Lightning.

away.name: Stuart Skinner
away.news: Impressive early-season performances from Stuart Skinner and Clay Stevenson made Connor Hellebuyck's (suspension) absence an afterthought, but recent struggles are keeping Winnipeg's crease uncertain. The Jets enter Thursday's game as +174 road underdogs against a Dallas Stars team with points in six of its last seven games (5-1-1).

home.name: Jake Oettinger
home.news: The Stars have struggled offensively at times to start the season, but they can point to Jake Oettinger's outstanding play as the reason for their 5-3-1 record. He saved 18 of 20 shots (.900 SV%) in his previous game, a 3-2 overtime win over the Boston Bruins. The Stars enter Thursday's divisional clash as sizeable -196 home favourites against a Winnipeg Jets team that has scored two or fewer goals in three of their last five games (1-3-1).

away.name: Jesper Wallstedt
away.news: Wallstedt has been busy with Filip Gustavsson (hip) sidelined and will return to the crease for the 10th time in Minnesota's first 11 games. That said, he is coming off his weakest performance of the season, allowing four goals on 32 shots (.875 SV%) in a 4-3 overtime loss to the Edmonton Oilers. Minnesota enters Thursday's contest as significant -202 road favourites against a Calgary Flames team coming off an impressive 3-2 win over the Carolina Hurricanes.

home.name: Devin Cooley
home.news: Cooley had a terrific first season as a full-time NHLer, serving primarily as Dustin Wolf's backup, posting a solid 2.69 GAA and .909 SV% in 31 appearances (10-10-6) for a poor Calgary Flames team. The 29-year-old Cooley struggled in his first two 2026-27 outings, but was excellent in his most recent game, saving 34 of 36 shots (.944 SV%) in a 3-2 win over the Carolina Hurricanes. He has a 4.01 GAA and .868 SV% in three games (1-2-0). The Flames enter Thursday's action as +180 home underdogs against a Minnesota Wild team on a three-game winning streak.

away.name: Brandon Bussi
away.news: The Hurricanes have leaned on Kochetkov for four of their last five games, but they will turn to Bussi on Thursday against the Edmonton Oilers. Bussi emerged from nowhere as a 27-year-old rookie in the 2025-26 season, leading the Hurricanes to a Stanley Cup, but he hasn't recaptured that brilliance in 2026-27. He has a 2.98 GAA and .882 SV in five games (2-2-1). The Hurricanes enter Thursday's contest as -117 road favourites against a 7-1-1 Oilers team.

home.name: Devon Levi
home.news: Heading into the 2026-27 season, the Oilers were turning to a goaltending tandem of Frederik Andersen and Tristan Jarry, but an injury to Andersen created an opening for Levi, who is making the most of his opportunity. Levi is coming off a strong performance, saving 37 of 30 shots (.900 SV%) in a 4-3 win over the Minnesota Wild. The 24-year-old goalie has a 2.00 GAA and .931 SV% in his last five games (4-1-0). The Oilers enter Thursday's contest as slight +106 home underdogs against a Carolina Hurricanes team that is 8-1-0 in their last nine games.
